security_distinctions.scalar_id: Registry lookup/correlation key. Existing source does not authenticate solely from scalar possession.
security_distinctions.stable_fingerprint: Separate 64-lowercase-hex SHA256 digest of domain-separated immutable projection. Detects projection mismatch only when checked through authenticated owner provenance; not a secret or bearer credential.
security_distinctions.hmac: Separate HMAC-SHA256 authentication with owner-local 32-byte secret, independent of scalar-ID entropy.
security_distinctions.exact_original_object: Prevents same-process reconstructed dataclass, JSON/copy, wrapper and subclass substitutions even when every scalar is copied.
security_distinctions.pid: Rejects live foreign process and fork inheritance. PID alone does not handle PID reuse; fresh process secret, empty registry and impossibility of original-object continuity provide that boundary.
security_distinctions.tombstone: Prevents duplicate issuance/reopening independently of ID encoding. A digest or long random ID does not by itself prevent stale replay.

conditions: Every authority-bearing operation authenticates the exact original typed owner/relation object in its private owner registry, current process and authenticated immutable graph before lookup results can confer authority.
Domain/PID/owner binding and current lifecycle state remain HMAC-authenticated; stable fingerprint and HMAC remain separate from the scalar.
Freshness/collision/reuse checks cover active records and permanent tombstones, with atomic allocation/publication under a private owner lock.
No string-only endpoint may acquire an original authoritative object or bypass the admission relation merely by presenting an ID.
A process restart/fork cannot reuse prior authoritative objects; scalar equality outside the retained namespace has no authority meaning.
Any future bearer boundary is a different security model and must not inherit this non-secret-handle conclusion without explicit requirement evolution.
future_preparation_implication.finite_counter_model: Semantically permissible if namespace, atomic increment, no rollback/reset/wrap, fail-closed exhaustion, permanent tombstones and process/owner separation are frozen. A counter's guessability does not defeat exact-original-object/HMAC checks. No generator is implemented here.
